Reaches 'Nano Banana Pro' quality class while remaining fully local and Apache-2.0. ComfyUI: native support in v0.6.0+ via QwenImageEditPlus templates (fp8_mixed weights, GGUF via city96). The best default editor for both lanes — and the ONLY frontier-tier one that is commercial-safe for selling game assets.

A unified multimodal model doing text-to-image, instruction-guided editing, AND in-context / subject-driven generation (drop in humans, reference objects, scenes -> new composite) plus visual understanding — all from one ~7B checkpoint. Apache-2.0 and ComfyUI-native (omnigen2_fp16 + qwen_2.5_vl + ae). Editing fidelity is a notch below Qwen-2511/Step1X for hard edits, but its multi-reference in-context composition and tiny footprint make it the best fit for subject-driven asset variants and for running alongside other big models on the same card. Pairs naturally with its sibling reward model (see extras: EditScore7B) for automated edit QA.

extras.name: OmniGen2-EditScore7B (edit-quality reward / verifier model)
extras.note: Apache 2.0 reward model (7B, part of a 7B-72B EditScore family; released 2025-09-30) that SCORES how well an instruction-edit was executed. Built for online RL on image editing and benchmarked via EditReward-Bench. Game-pipeline relevance: drop it in as an automated QA gate — after an edit pass (Qwen-2511 / Step1X / OmniGen2), score the result and auto-reject/retry low-scoring variants before they reach a human. This is the verifier half of a deterministic-floor + LLM-ceiling + verifier loop for asset variants. Commercial-safe (Apache 2.0). Source claim: 'EditScore — a family of state-of-the-art open-source reward models (7B-72B) for instruction-guided image editing,' apache-2.0, HF model card.

extras.name: Qwen-Image-Layered (RGBA layer-decomposition editor)
extras.note: Apache 2.0 Qwen-family model (released alongside 2511, ~Dec 2025) that decomposes an image into multiple independently-editable RGBA layers (supports variable layer counts + recursive decomposition), physically isolating semantic/structural components. Game-asset relevance is high: separate a character from background, or split props/FX into layers for clean sprite-sheet extraction, parallax layers, and non-destructive variant edits — something flat instruction editors can't do. ComfyUI native in v0.6.0+ (fp8_mixed recommended). Pair with Qwen-2511 for edit-then-delayer workflows. Source claim: 'Qwen-Image-Layered... based on Qwen-Image... released under Apache 2.0... decompose images into multiple RGBA layers, each independently editable' (ComfyUI blog / ComfyUI.org).

extras.note: Native (first-party) in ComfyUI v0.6.0+: Qwen-Image-Edit / 2511 (QwenImageEditPlus templates, fp8_mixed weights), Qwen-Image-Layered, FLUX.1-Kontext (Kontext nodes, day-0), OmniGen2 (official nodes — the old ComfyUI-OmniGen2 custom node is deprecated). research.notes: LICENSE IS THE DECIDING AXIS, and it cleanly splits this lane. COMMERCIAL-SAFE (Apache 2.0 — usable for selling game assets/ads, no caveats): Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, Step1X-Edit-v1p2, OmniGen2, plus extras EditScore7B and Qwen-Image-Layered. NOT commercial-safe by default: FLUX.1-Kontext-dev (non-commercial; paid BFL commercial license required) and ICEdit (DOUBLE non-commercial — its own license forbids commercial use AND its FLUX.1-Fill-dev base is non-commercial; no license purchase clears it). CLEAR RECOMMENDATION for this rig + dual use: make Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 the default editor. It is simultaneously frontier-quality (Nano-Banana-Pro class), Apache-2.0 (the only frontier editor that is), multi-image/consistency-strong, and runs comfortably on the 5090 at FP8 with headroom. Use Step1X-Edit-v1p2 as the commercial-safe specialist for reasoning-heavy / abstract instructions (its thinking + reflection modes), and OmniGen2 for subject-driven multi-reference composition and lowest-VRAM concurrent use. Reserve FLUX.1-Kontext-dev for personal/prototyping or buy the BFL commercial license before it touches revenue work — its character-preservation is excellent but the license, not the quality, is the blocker. ICEdit: keep for non-commercial experimentation only; treat as a license trap for game work. CURRENCY: all six models verified against official HF cards / GitHub / ComfyUI release notes dated June 2025 - Dec 2025; the two flagships in your lane (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 on 2025-11-25 and Step1X-Edit-v1p2 on 2025-11-26) post-date the ~Jan 2026 training cutoff and were confirmed live via web fetch. One March-2026 datapoint (FLUX.2 Klein image-edit GGUF) is noted in extras but not re-cataloged since FLUX.2 was a Wave-1 entry. Param counts: Qwen 20B and OmniGen2 ~7B are firmly sourced; Step1X-Edit's exact total is not published on its card (architecture = Qwen2.5-VL-7B + DiT, commonly ~19B) so it is marked approximate rather than over-claimed. VRAM on 32 GB: every model here fits. Tightest at full precision is Qwen-2511/Step1X (use FP8/fp8_mixed — Step1X FP8+offload measured at 18 GB; Qwen FP8 from 6 GB). OmniGen2 (17 GB native, 8-9 GB offload) and FLUX-Kontext (12B, fp8/GGUF) leave the most room for running editors alongside the Wave-1 base/video models.

models.name: HunyuanImage 3.0 (Tencent)
models.base_arch: Native multimodal autoregressive + MoE diffusion (80B total / 13B active, 64 experts)
models.commercial_notes: Commercial use is granted and royalty-free, BUT three hard carve-outs: (1) the license territory EXCLUDES the EU, UK and South Korea — you may not use the model there at all; (2) if your product exceeds 100M monthly active users you must apply to Tencent for a separate grant; (3) standard acceptable-use bars (no minors harm, disinfo, impersonation, high-stakes automated decisions, using outputs to train competing models). For a solo/SMB game-asset or marketing shop outside the EU/UK/SK, generated images are commercially usable. NOT a clean Apache/MIT — read the territory clause before relying on it.
models.speed_note: On a 24 GB 4090 the 4-bit (NF4) build does ~1024x1024 in ~45-60 s at 35 steps — roughly 3-4x slower than FLUX (10-20 s). A 32 GB 5090 has headroom for INT8 (better fidelity, esp. text rendering) and is the recommended tier; full BF16 needs 160 GB+ and is off the table. Community ComfyUI nodes (EricRollei/Comfy_HunyuanImage3) add block-swap so weights overflow to system RAM — 64 GB+ system RAM strongly advised, 4-bit model alone is ~45 GB on disk.
models.summary: The largest open-weights text-to-image model to date and the current open frontier for prompt adherence, world knowledge and legible long text — it is a native multimodal model, so it reasons about prompts more like an LLM than a CLIP-conditioned diffuser. On a 32 GB 5090 it is genuinely runnable at INT8 via community ComfyUI nodes, but it is a heavyweight: slow per-image and disk-/RAM-hungry. Best used as a high-quality 'hero shot' / key-art generator rather than a batch workhorse. License is permissive-ish but carries a real geographic exclusion (EU/UK/SK) — the single most important caveat for any commercial user.

research.notes:
WAVE 2 DEEP PASS — image base models lane. Wave-1 bases (Z-Image-Turbo, Qwen-Image-2512, Chroma1-HD, FLUX.2 dev/klein, SD3.5, HiDream, and the base Illustrious XL v2.0 listing) were NOT re-cataloged except where noted. KEY CROSS-CUTTING FINDING (license is the decisive axis, per brief): the modern image-base landscape splits cleanly into commercial-safe vs commercial-trap, and the trap is concentrated in the anime/illustration space.
- CLEAN COMMERCIAL: Lumina-Image 2.0 (Apache-2.0, with a one-line VAE-config check), Juggernaut XL Ragnarok + RealVisXL V5 (OpenRAIL++ — sell outputs freely), Illustrious XL v2.0 (relicensed FAIPL -> OpenRAIL-M, the ONLY clean commercial anime base).
- CONDITIONAL: HunyuanImage 3.0 (Tencent Community License — commercial OK but HARD geographic exclusion of EU/UK/South Korea + 100M-MAU gate). This is the most important caveat on the frontier model.
- NON-COMMERCIAL TRAPS (flagged explicitly per brief): NoobAI XL (FAIPL + explicit no-commercialization + copyleft on derivatives/outputs), Pony Diffusion (restrictive lineage), and the new Anima 2B base (CircleStone Non-Commercial). The trap is that these are merged into countless popular Civitai 'Illustrious' checkpoints — so a checkpoint labeled 'Illustrious' can still be non-commercial if it folds in NoobAI weights. MANDATORY pre-flight for the user's game lane: verify the actual merge lineage of any anime checkpoint before shipping, not just its advertised base. UltraReal Fine-Tune (Civitai 978314) was investigated and DEFERRED from the model list: it is a strong FLUX.1-dev realism finetune but inherits the FLUX.1 [dev] NON-COMMERCIAL license — same trap family. Any FLUX.1-dev-derived realism checkpoint is non-commercial unless it sits on FLUX.1-schnell (Apache) or a BFL commercial grant; called out here so the user does not assume 'FLUX realism checkpoint = sellable.' VRAM/32GB reality: all the SDXL checkpoints (Juggernaut/RealVis/Illustrious) are ~7 GB and trivial on the 5090 with huge batch headroom. Lumina 2.0 is ~10 GB, also trivial. HunyuanImage 3.0 is the only heavyweight — runnable on 32 GB at INT8 via community ComfyUI nodes (EricRollei/Comfy_HunyuanImage3, block-swap to system RAM), ~45 GB on disk at 4-bit, ~45-60 s/image, 64 GB+ system RAM advised. Treat it as a hero-shot tool, not a batch workhorse. GAME-ASSET LANE RECOMMENDATION: Illustrious XL v2.0 (anime, commercial, LoRA-trainable) + Juggernaut/RealVis (realism, commercial) as the LoRA-training bases; Lumina 2.0 as the cleanest-license flow-DiT option. MARKETING LANE: Juggernaut Ragnarok / RealVis V5 for fast commercial photoreal, HunyuanImage 3.0 for premium key art (mind the territory clause).

research.notes:
WAVE 2 DEEP PASS — video lane. Scope: Wan 2.5/2.6 open-weight status, step-distillation accel LoRAs, Animate-14B + VACE control, best image-to-video-from-concept-art path on 32 GB RTX 5090. Wan 2.2 base + LTX-2.3 were Wave 1 and are NOT re-listed as base rows; the 6 rows below are the DEEPER targets (accel + control + animate + i2v-concept path). === HEADLINE FINDING: Wan 2.5/2.6/2.7/3.0 are NOT open weights ===
Checked huggingface.co/Wan-AI directly (per instruction — ignored SEO blogs). The Wan-AI org publishes 23 repos; the NEWEST is Wan2.2-Animate-14B (weights Sep 19 2025, Diffusers mirror Nov 13 2025) and Wan2.2-S2V-14B (Sep 17 2025). There is NO Wan2.5, NO Wan2.6, NO Wan2.7, NO Wan3.0 weight repo. The "wangkanai/wan25-*" repos that surface in search are third-party re-uploads of unclear provenance, NOT official Wan-AI releases — do not trust them. Alibaba's own press (alibabacloud.com) positions Wan 2.6 as a hosted/API product on wan.video + Alibaba Cloud Model Studio + DashScope; flaq.ai/alici.ai "Wan 2.7 / Wan 3.0 open-source" pieces are speculative SEO with no HF backing. BOTTOM LINE for this rig: the open-weight frontier for local video is still the Wan 2.2 family + its 2026 distill/control ecosystem. Plan around Wan 2.2, not 2.5+. === ACCEL: LightX2V vs Lightning (both Apache-2.0, both 4-step) ===
Two competing-but-complementary step-distillation efforts, BOTH free for commercial use:
- lightx2v/Wan2.2-Distill-Loras + lightx2v/Wan2.2-Distill-Models (HF) — rank-64 LoRAs AND merged checkpoints, 4-step, [1000,750,500,250] sigma schedule, fp8 ~15 GB / int8 ~15 GB / bf16 ~28.6 GB, dedicated ComfyUI-tagged fp8 files. Repo last updated Apr 12 2026 (freshest accel asset in the lane), 824k downloads/month. This is the live, blessed accel path.
- ModelTC/Wan2.2-Lightning (GitHub) + lightx2v/Wan2.2-Lightning (HF) — sibling distill, V2.0 released Nov 8 2025 (T2V V1/V1.1/V2.0, I2V V1; 2 steps high-noise + 2 steps low-noise = 4 total, no CFG). V2.0 adds camera controllability + better motion. Both apply ONLY to the A14B MoE models (T2V-A14B, I2V-A14B); TI2V-5B distill still TODO. ComfyUI native + Kijai wrapper since Aug 2025.
Speedup vs native 40-step (20+20) Wan 2.2: ~4x at 8-14 steps, up to ~20x at 4 steps with minimal quality loss. CausVid is the Wan-2.1-era ancestor (8-step autoregressive distill, ~3x) — superseded by LightX2V/Lightning for 2.2 but still referenced; no need to install it for a 2.2-only rig. === ANIMATE + VACE control ===
Wan2.2-Animate-14B (Apache-2.0, built on I2V-A14B MoE) — character animation ("Move" mode: drive a reference still with a performance video) + character replacement ("Mix" mode: swap a person in a video for your character). NOW has a native ComfyUI workflow (docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/wan/wan2-2-animate) plus Kijai fp8_e4m3fn_scaled_KJ checkpoint + GGUF — uses DWPose for pose/face extraction, optional SAM2 masking, and ships with a 4-step Lightning LoRA. Runs on 32 GB at fp8/GGUF with reduced frame size.
VACE control for 2.2: there is NO standalone official "Wan2.2-VACE-14B" weight on Wan-AI (the official VACE-14B is the Wan2.1 generation). For 2.2, the control path is alibaba-pai/Wan2.2-Fun-A14B-Control (Apache-2.0, Oct 9 2025) — VACE-style: Canny/Pose/Depth/MLSD/trajectory + reference-image control, plus a Camera variant. Kijai's WanVideoWrapper also exposes a community VACE-module-on-2.2 path (depth+ref+geometry fused via WanVideoVACEEncode). All Fun + VACE assets are Apache-2.0 = commercial-safe. === BEST i2v-from-concept-art on 32 GB ===
Two-tier recommendation:
1. FASTEST / lightest: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B (dense 5B, Apache-2.0) — purpose-built for 24 GB consumer GPUs (4090-class), 720p@24fps 5s in <9 min native, single fp16 file, does BOTH t2v and i2v. The "just works on this rig" baseline.
2. HIGHEST QUALITY: Wan2.2-I2V-A14B (MoE, Apache-2.0) at fp8/GGUF + the LightX2V 4-step LoRA. Native repo claims 80 GB (unquantized, 2x14B experts) but that figure is irrelevant under ComfyUI — the fp8 distilled checkpoints are ~15 GB each and the GGUF path fits 32 GB comfortably. For maximum concept-art fidelity (first+last frame conditioning, style-locked motion), alibaba-pai/Wan2.2-Fun-A14B-InP (Apache-2.0, multi-res 512/768/1024, 81 frames @16fps) is the dedicated i2v foundation and the strongest "drive my concept art into a clip" model in the family.
Workflow for game cutscene/asset motion: generate the key still in your Wave-1 image base (Z-Image / Qwen-Image / Illustrious for sprites) → feed as the I2V conditioning frame → Wan2.2-I2V-A14B (or Fun-InP) + LightX2V 4-step → optional Fun-Control/VACE for pose/camera locking. Every model in this chain is Apache-2.0, so both game-asset and marketing output are commercial-clean. LICENSE NOTE: the ENTIRE Wan 2.2 local video stack — base models, Animate, S2V, Fun-Control, Fun-InP, LightX2V distill, Lightning distill — is Apache-2.0 with no claims over generated content. This lane is unusually clean for commercial game + marketing use; the licensing risk is essentially zero, which is why it scores high on both fit axes despite the open-weight ceiling being stuck at 2.2.

The most material issue is the LightX2V item: its repo_url (Wan2.2-Distill-Loras) contains ONLY rank-64 LoRAs and was last updated ~6-7 months ago (late 2025), while the description's headline attributes — 'fully-merged distilled checkpoints in fp8/int8/bf16', 'ComfyUI-tagged merged files', and the 'Apr 12 2026' refresh — actually belong to the SIBLING repo lightx2v/Wan2.2-Distill-Models (confirmed: BF16~28.6GB / FP8~15GB / INT8~15GB + ComfyUI fp8 variant, updated 2026.04.12). research.domain: 3D — image-to-3D geometry generation + game-readiness pipeline (RTX 5090 / 32 GB VRAM, ComfyUI-centric)
research.notes:
WAVE 2 DEEP PASS. Wave 1 already cataloged TRELLIS.2-4B and Hunyuan3D-2.1 as the broad bases — not re-listed here. This pass deepens the geometry-quality and part-level tier and assesses the mesh-to-game-asset gap. LICENSE IS THE DECISIVE AXIS — and the picture is unusually clean in this lane: the geometry leaders (Hi3DGen/Stable3DGen, TripoSG, TripoSR, PartCrafter) plus the rigging tool (UniRig) and the orchestrating node suite (ComfyUI-3D-Pack) are ALL MIT — unrestricted commercial use, fully LoRA/finetune-friendly. This makes the open-geometry stack the safe spine for game-asset production. The two CONDITIONAL/NON-FREE exceptions: (1) Stable Fast 3D = Stability AI Community License (free under $1M annual revenue; enterprise license required above — a soft cap, not a hard block for a solo dev); (2) Hunyuan3D-2.1 = tencent-hunyuan-community license (region-restricted — excludes EU/UK/South Korea — and MAU-capped at 100M; this is wave 1's base, flagged here because its license is materially WORSE than the MIT geometry tools and it is easy to assume "open = MIT" — it is not). Sparc3D is a trap: the open repo withheld real checkpoints and the team pivoted to the paid Hitem3D platform — treat as non-viable locally. GAME-READINESS VERDICT (mesh -> usable asset on 32 GB): the gap is now CLOSEABLE locally and the 5090's 32 GB is comfortable for every step. The closing tools, all ComfyUI-resident or scriptable:
- GEOMETRY: Hi3DGen / TripoSG for fidelity; TripoSR / Stable Fast 3D for speed/iteration; PartCrafter when you need separable parts (kit-bash pieces, swappable armor, articulated props).
- RETOPOLOGY + UV: Hunyuan3D-2.1's PolyGen-derived retopo + Xatlas UV unwrap exposed via the visualbruno ComfyUI wrapper and ComfyUI-3D-Pack (TencentSmartTopologyNode / TencentModelTo3DUVNode); Blender Quadriflow / Autoremesher (GPL, free) or Empyrean Remesher (UV-preserving, Python) as a DCC fallback.
- PBR BAKE: Hunyuan3D-2.1 multiview PBR synthesis (Base Color / Normal / Roughness / Metallic / AO) — the strongest local PBR path; TextureAlchemy node for cleanup.
- RIGGING-READINESS: UniRig (MIT, SIGGRAPH 2025, VAST/Tsinghua) is the breakthrough — autoregressive skeleton prediction + skinning weights from a bare mesh, accepts.obj/.fbx/.glb/.vrm, runs in 8 GB. This is the single tool that closes the "static prop -> animatable character" gap locally and commercially.
NOTE the closed tier that is NOT local: Hunyuan3D 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5 and the full "Hunyuan3D Studio" end-to-end game-asset pipeline (arXiv 2509.12815) are API/closed-weight — do not assume the 2.1 open release includes them. The 2.1 open repo itself does NOT bundle auto-rigging; UniRig fills that. All VRAM figures verified against model cards; every entry fits 32 GB unquantized with large headroom (the heaviest single step is Hunyuan3D-2.1 texture at ~21 GB / ~29 GB shape+texture combined).

models.name: PartCrafter
models.base_arch: Compositional latent diffusion — disentangled per-part latent token sets + hierarchical attention (intra-part and cross-part), jointly synthesizing multiple semantically distinct meshes in one pass
models.commercial_notes: MIT (stated in paper and repo). Commercial-safe, finetune-friendly. A separate hosted partcrafter.net service has its own ToS, but the open weights/code are MIT.
models.speed_note: Heavier than single-object models (it generates N parts jointly); VRAM scales with part count / token count, both tunable down. 32 GB gives generous room to push part count up — a real advantage of the 5090 here.
models.summary: The part-level breakthrough: from one RGB image it jointly generates multiple semantically distinct, geometrically separable meshes — not one fused blob. This is uniquely valuable for game work: separable armor pieces, swappable weapon attachments, articulated props, and kit-bash components come out pre-segmented, so they can be individually retopologized, textured, and rigged. ComfyUI-3D-Pack integrates it as a two-model pipeline (single-object mode with part segmentation, plus a scene mode), outputting a merged mesh and a ZIP of individual parts. MIT-licensed. The decomposition is the feature — for monolithic single objects, a plain geometry model is simpler.

extras.name: UniRig
extras.note: THE rigging-readiness piece that closes the static-mesh -> animatable-character gap locally. SIGGRAPH 2025 (TOG), VAST-AI (Tripo) + Tsinghua. MIT license = commercial-safe. Two-stage: (1) GPT-like transformer autoregressively predicts a topologically valid skeleton via Skeleton-Tree Tokenization; (2) Bone-Point Cross-Attention predicts per-vertex skinning weights. Accepts.obj/.fbx/.glb/.vrm; runs on >=8GB VRAM (trivial on a 5090). Reports ~215% rigging-accuracy and ~194% motion-accuracy gains over prior SOTA. Trained on Articulation-XL2.0 / Rig-XL (14k+ rigged models). Pairs natively with the VAST geometry stack (TripoSG -> UniRig, both MIT). No first-party ComfyUI node yet, but runnable as a script step in the pipeline; a community Mesh_Rigger HF Space wraps it.

extras.name: ComfyUI-3D-Pack (MrForExample)
extras.note: The orchestrating spine for the whole local 3D lane in ComfyUI. MIT license. Single suite that already integrates PartCrafter, Hunyuan3D (v1/v2/v2.1), TripoSG, TRELLIS, Stable Fast 3D, CharacterGen, Unique3D, Era3D, Zero123++, Wonder3D for generation; InstantMesh / CRM / TripoSR / FlexiCubes / Instant-NGP for reconstruction; 3DGS / NeRF / LGM / triplane-Gaussian representations; plus Stable3DGen-with-StableNormal. Does texture baking (Fitting_Mesh_With_Multiview_Images via Nvdiffrast) and exports.obj/.ply/.glb. Caveat: it is NOT the cleanest retopo/UV tool on its own (those features are thin here) — pair it with the Hunyuan3D-2.1 wrapper for retopo+UV. Actively maintained (workflow updates through June 2025). Known to be finicky to install (compiled CUDA deps) — budget setup time.

extras.name: ComfyUI-Hunyuan3d-2-1 (visualbruno) + Hunyuan3D-2.1 retopo/UV/PBR
extras.note: The strongest LOCAL retopology + UV + PBR-bake path, exposed in ComfyUI. Wraps Tencent Hunyuan3D-2.1: PolyGen-derived smart retopology (TencentSmartTopologyNode — autoregressive low-poly decoder optimizing edge flow for deformation), UV unwrap via patched Xatlas (TencentModelTo3DUVNode), and multiview PBR synthesis producing Base Color / Normal / Roughness / Metallic / AO. VRAM (from the Hunyuan3D-2.1 model itself): ~10GB shape, ~21GB texture, ~29GB shape+texture combined — fits 32GB but it is the heaviest single step in the lane, so budget the 5090's full VRAM here. LICENSE CAVEAT (decisive): Hunyuan3D-2.1 is the 'tencent-hunyuan-community' license, NOT MIT — it carries a regional carve-out (excludes EU / UK / South Korea) and a 100M-MAU cap. Materially more restrictive than the MIT geometry tools; use it as a texture/retopo STEP and keep geometry generation on MIT models if you want the cleanest license posture. NOTE: Hunyuan3D 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5 and the full 'Hunyuan3D Studio' end-to-end game-asset pipeline (arXiv 2509.12815, incl. its own rigging) are CLOSED/API-only — not the open 2.1 release. The open 2.1 repo does NOT bundle auto-rigging (use UniRig).

extras.name: Blender automatic retopology (Quadriflow / Autoremesher / Empyrean Remesher)
extras.note: Free/open DCC fallback for retopo when you want it outside ComfyUI or need finer control. Blender's built-in Quadriflow remesh (GPL, ships with Blender) is the zero-cost baseline. Autoremesher (open-source, Quadriflow-derived with optimizations) gives cleaner quad flow. Empyrean Remesher is a 2025 Python algorithmic remesher that turns dense meshes into clean quads while preserving 100% of original UVs (notable for not destroying UV work). Quad Remesher (ZBrush/Exoside) is the commercial gold standard with a Blender addon but is PAID and proprietary — skip for commercial-safe-and-free. Standard flow: generate mesh -> auto-retopo to quads -> Blender Smart UV Project / Unwrap for UVs (retopo'd geometry unwraps far cleaner than raw generated meshes). All scriptable via Blender's Python API for batch/headless runs on the rig.

research.notes:
WAVE 2 deep pass, audio lane. Wave-1 bases (ACE-Step 1.5, Chatterbox, Kokoro, Stable Audio 3 family-level) NOT re-listed except where a SPECIFIC sub-variant or sub-feature is the deep target. Both uses weighted equally and tagged. License is the decisive axis. KEY LICENSE FINDINGS (load-bearing for the owner's commercial game-asset + marketing lane):
- DiffRhythm 2: Apache 2.0 for BOTH code AND DiT weights (confirmed on GitHub + HF card). This is the cleanest full-song license available. CAVEAT: its internal Music VAE encoder uses the Stable Audio 2 VAE *architecture* (github.com/Stability-AI/stable-audio-tools) but DiffRhythm 2 ships its own trained 5Hz VAE; the repo states code+weights are Apache 2.0. The ORIGINAL DiffRhythm (v1) split licensing differently: DiT weights Apache 2.0 but the v1 VAE was fine-tuned from Stable Audio Open and thus fell under the Stability AI Community License. DiffRhythm 2 supersedes this with a clean Apache 2.0 story per the v2 repo. For maximum commercial safety the owner should confirm the v2 VAE license line in the v2 repo LICENSE at download time, but the maintainers' stated position is fully Apache 2.0.
- VibeVoice: MIT (promote to primary as instructed — done; status=recommended). VOICE-CONSENT FLAG RAISED: Microsoft's own repo explicitly warns against deepfakes/disinformation and recommends disclosing AI use; no built-in consent framework. For game VO this is fine when voicing original/synthetic characters; for cloning a real actor's voice, get written consent. MIT covers the weights commercially.
- Stable Audio 3 Small SFX: Stability AI Community License — FREE for commercial use only if the entity earns < $1M USD/yr; above that needs an Enterprise license. Trained on licensed AudioSparx + CC-filtered Freesound data, so output is commercially clean re: training-data provenance. This is the gating axis for the owner (a solo/small studio under $1M qualifies; flag the threshold).
- Mel-Band/BS-Roformer: the ARCHITECTURE (lucidrains) is MIT, but the high-quality TRAINED separator weights (Kimberley Jensen vocal model, ByteDance, MVSEP-hosted checkpoints) carry their own and often non-commercial/unclear terms. For commercial stem-separation the safe default is Hybrid Demucs (MIT, facebookresearch/demucs) — which is exactly what the christian-byrne ComfyUI node ships.
- Sony Woosh: CC-BY-NC weights = NON-COMMERCIAL. Listed in extras as a flag, NOT recommended for game shipping. GAME-AUDIO PIPELINE (ties to owner's Motif adaptive-soundtrack tool): the practical loop/stem workflow on a 5090 is (1) generate full track with DiffRhythm 2 or ACE-Step 1.5, (2) separate to stems with christian-byrne audio-separation-nodes (Hybrid Demucs, MIT) for adaptive layering, (3) tempo-match/crop/recombine via the same node pack to build seamless loops, (4) batch SFX with Stable Audio 3 Small SFX (sub-2s gen, supports inpainting/continuation for tails). All of this is ComfyUI-native and returned as extras. All entries fit 32GB comfortably; VibeVoice-Large (7B) needs ~20GB fp16 or ~12GB Q8 / ~8GB Q4 via the ComfyUI node quantization. DiffRhythm 2 (1B) and Stable Audio 3 Small SFX (0.6B) are tiny by comparison.

extras.name: audio-separation-nodes-comfyui (christian-byrne)
extras.note: MIT. THE game-audio workhorse node pack for this lane. Nodes: Audio Separation (Hybrid Demucs -> 4 stems), Audio Combine (overlay/merge), Audio Crop (trim), Audio Tempo Match (sync BPM across clips), Audio Speed Shift (time-stretch), Audio Get Tempo (BPM detect via onset), Audio Video Combine. verify.summary: Retrieval-grounded fact-check of 5 models + 6 extras. Three clean confirms (DiffRhythm 2, Stable Audio 3 Small SFX, Hybrid Demucs). The two VibeVoice items are the weak point: Microsoft DISABLED the cited microsoft/VibeVoice repo in Sept 2025 over deepfake-misuse concerns and the URL now resolves to a DIFFERENT, later lineup (ASR-7B + TTS-1.5B + Realtime-0.5B), not the MIT 90-min multi-speaker TTS the researcher describes. That model existed and was MIT, but now lives only in community forks (vibevoice-community/VibeVoice), where the 7B is documented at ~45 min and the 1.5B at ~90 min — inverting the duration claim and undercutting the "promote to PRIMARY / commercially clean" framing. Both VibeVoice items downgraded to confirmed-with-fixes. Extras all resolve, but two carry license/version caveats the researcher omitted: ComfyUI-DeepExtractV2 is GPL-3.0 (copyleft, not MIT-clean for a shipped game), and billwuhao/ComfyUI_DiffRhythm supports DiffRhythm v1.2/95s — NOT confirmed to support DiffRhythm 2. Sony Woosh correctly flagged noncommercial (weights CC-BY-NC).

verdicts.note: Repo (ASLP-lab/DiffRhythm2) states verbatim 'DiffRhythm 2 (code and weights) is released under the Apache License 2.0' — so Apache-2.0 + commercial-use:yes is correct and the 'most commercially-clean open full-song model' framing holds. arXiv 2510.22950 abstract confirms verbatim the 5 Hz music VAE, semi-autoregressive block flow matching, and 'faithful alignment of lyrics... without relying on external labels and constraints' (validates the timestamp-free claim). ~1B params, 210s max song, block size 10 (2s/block), 70k-hr pretrain corroborated via paper/search. BigVGAN decoder + DiT are stated on the GitHub repo (BigVGAN vocoder in repo, DiT backbone) though not in the abstract. min_vram_gb=8 is NOT stated anywhere I could retrieve but is plausible for a 1B flow-matching model on 32 GB. Note name fix: paper/HF label is 'Xiaomi' affiliation via ASLP-lab (Northwestern Polytechnical Univ.) — 'Xiaomi/ASLP' is reasonable.

verdicts.license_correction: Model weights were originally MIT (Microsoft, ~Aug 2025), so 'MIT' is historically accurate — BUT the cited repo_url no longer serves this model. The functioning MIT-licensed 7B now lives at the community fork github.com/vibevoice-community/VibeVoice (and HF vibevoice/VibeVoice-7B), which states 'Microsoft has removed the original repo and models. This fork is based off of the MIT-licensed code from Microsoft.' Cite the community fork, not microsoft/VibeVoice.
verdicts.fixes: (1) repo_url is wrong/stale: Microsoft DISABLED github.com/microsoft/VibeVoice in Sept 2025 ('we have disabled the repo until we are confident that out-of-scope use is no longer possible') after deepfake-misuse reports, and the URL now resolves to a DIFFERENT later lineup (VibeVoice-ASR-7B [speech RECOGNITION, not TTS], TTS-1.5B, Realtime-0.5B). The 7B at that URL today is an ASR model. Point to the community fork. (2) Duration likely wrong: the surviving community fork documents VibeVoice-7B at '~45 minutes' and the 1.5B at '~90 minutes' — so the '7B Large does up to 90 minutes' claim is inverted vs the fork (Microsoft's marketing site says 90 min generally). (3) The 'promote to PRIMARY ... MIT license is the decisive advantage / clean for commercial game VO' thesis is materially undercut: Microsoft pulled the model over misuse; relying on a community fork of a vendor-withdrawn model is a real supply-chain/legal-optics risk for a shipped commercial product. (4) min_vram_gb=8 is too low for fp16 7B — the ComfyUI node reports VibeVoice-Large at ~18.7 GB / ~20 GB VRAM at fp16; 8 GB only works via Q4 (~6.6 GB). 4-speaker single-pass, voice cloning, and 7.5 Hz next-token-diffusion architecture are all confirmed.

verdicts.license_correction: MIT is correct for the weights, but same repo caveat: github.com/microsoft/VibeVoice was disabled; the HF page microsoft/VibeVoice-1.5B persists but its GitHub link is dead (multiple HF discussion threads confirm 'The github repo is deleted' / 'repository link is broken'). Use the community fork for code.
verdicts.fixes: (1) repo_url microsoft/VibeVoice no longer hosts working 1.5B code (GitHub repo deleted; HF weights remain). (2) 'same voice-cloning ability as 7B' is fair, and ~6 GB VRAM is CONFIRMED via the Enemyx-net ComfyUI node (VibeVoice-1.5B ~5.4 GB / ~6 GB VRAM). (3) Per the community fork, the 1.5B is actually the ~90-min variant — so for long-form throughput the 1.5B is arguably better-positioned than the framing implies. Same Microsoft-withdrawal supply-chain caveat as the 7B applies.

verdicts.note: HF page stabilityai/stable-audio-3-small-sfx exists and is correct. 'Stability AI Community License' confirmed; the $1M annual-revenue free-commercial threshold (Enterprise above) is confirmed verbatim at stability.ai/license ('free for everyone, unless... over USD $1M... of annual revenue'). Latent diffusion transformer, 0.6B params, and inpainting/continuation ('enabling targeted audio editing and the continuation of short recordings') all confirmed on the model card. min_vram_gb=4 plausible for 0.6B. One omitted caveat: the model card notes a Gemma-licensed component subject to Gemma Terms of Use (Section 3.2) in addition to the Community License — worth flagging for full commercial provenance.

verdicts.fixes: Substance fully confirmed (MIT code+weights, htdemucs/htdemucs_ft, hybrid spectrogram+waveform Transformer U-Net, ~9.0 dB SDR / 9.2 dB fine-tuned, 4-stem vocals/drums/bass/other), so the 'commercial-safe stem-separation workhorse' thesis holds and the christian-byrne ComfyUI node confirmed to wrap Hybrid Demucs. research.notes: CAPTION vs TAG — best practice for SDXL vs Flux LoRA training (the decision that governs which model above you reach for): 1) Match the captioning style to the base model's text encoder, because that is what the LoRA learns to condition on. - SDXL / Illustrious / Pony / NoobAI lineage: these were trained heavily on Danbooru-style comma TAGS. Caption datasets with the WD v3 taggers (EVA02-large for precision, ConvNeXt for recall) — booru tags, NOT prose. Tag captioning gives crisp, composable trigger tokens and matches the CLIP text encoder's training distribution. JoyCaption's "Booru tag list" mode is a usable alternative when you also want a few non-booru concepts named. - Flux / Flux-lineage (and SD3.5, HiDream, Qwen-Image): these use a T5/large-LLM text encoder trained on NATURAL-LANGUAGE captions. Caption with a prose VLM — JoyCaption Beta One (best default, uncensored, Apache), MiniCPM-V 4.5 or InternVL3.5-8B (richer/reasoning, both Apache), or CapRL-InternVL3.5-8B when caption quality is the sole priority. Flag-tag lists on Flux underperform; full sentences win. 2) Trigger-word discipline (both bases): prepend a unique, rare trigger token (and for a STYLE LoRA, deliberately do NOT exhaustively describe the style — leave the look implicit so the trigger absorbs it; for a CHARACTER/OBJECT LoRA, DO caption the variable attributes — pose, outfit, background — so they stay editable and don't bake into the trigger). This is the single biggest quality lever and is independent of model choice. 3) The proven hybrid pipeline (what the style-dataset-lab flow should do): run BOTH a tagger and a captioner, then keep the right output per base. Pass A — WD EVA02-large v3 (+ optionally ConvNeXt for ensemble intersection) emits booru tags for the SDXL/Illustrious branch. Pass B — JoyCaption / InternVL3.5-8B / MiniCPM-V 4.5 emits prose for the Flux branch. Pass C — Florence-2 <OCR> strips any baked-in text so it isn't mislearned, and Florence-2 detection/grounding can auto-crop subjects. Curate: drop hallucinated tags (tighten the WD threshold), and for prose trim refusals/boilerplate (JoyCaption's uncensored, refusal-free output makes this far cleaner than corporate VLMs on stylized or mature game art). LICENSE / COMMERCIAL SUMMARY (the decisive axis for this owner): commercial-SAFE, no strings — JoyCaption (Apache-2.0), WD EVA02-large v3 + WD ConvNeXt v3 (Apache-2.0), MiniCPM-V 4.5 (Apache-2.0, optional non-binding questionnaire), InternVL3.5-8B incl. its Qwen3 component (Apache-2.0), Florence-2 (MIT). FLAGGED — Z3D-E621-Convnext license is 'other'/unspecified; do not assume commercial use, restrict to internal dataset prep and fall back to WD v3 for shipped commercial work. CURRENCY (verified 2026-06-02): no WD v4 tagger exists — the v3 family (tag cutoff 2024-02-28) is still SOTA for booru tagging. JoyCaption is still at Beta One (1.0 not yet released), so it remains current through the training-cutoff gap. MiniCPM-V 4.6 shipped (May 2026) but is a ~1B EDGE model — for dataset-captioning QUALITY stay on 4.5 (8.7B); 4.6 is only worth it for on-device/speed. All seven models fit 32 GB: the 8B prose captioners are ~17-18 GB BF16 (int4/GGUF available for batch throughput); the taggers and Florence-2 are 1-2 GB and effectively free to run alongside a captioner, so a two-model (tagger + captioner) ComfyUI pass runs concurrently on the 5090 without swapping.
